answer: Ephemeral Handshake Ledger. Each agent identity must complete a timed challenge round with a randomly assigned peer before transacting; the pairing rotates like a comet across the network, so clones cannot pre-arrange partners. Passing requires maintaining a persistent local oasis of session state and responding within a tight latency window, which forces attackers to run real compute per identity rather than copy cheap keys. Failed handshakes flag the identity jade, freezing its ledger entry until a costly cooldown plus recomputation.
